fig_causal_chain_overview: From item-level acquiescence to model-level homogenization. A four-stage causal chain that explains why every standard psychometric validity check fails on LLMs. Stage 1 (item): alignment training produces an agree-impulse with directional asymmetry — IPIP normal items Δ = +0.29, SD3 dark-trait items Δ = −0.33. Stage 2 (domain): reverse-keyed items behave like forward items so Cronbach's α tracks reverse-item density at Spearman ρ = −1.0 across IPIP Big Five. Stage 3 (structural): EFA collapses the expected 5 Big Five factors into 3 universally across 20 LLMs (Tucker's φ = 0.993). Stage 4 (model): inter-model variance falls below 1% on both Likert and binary composites, making cross-model personality comparisons statistically meaningless at this resolution. A side panel lists the diagnostic battery: 4 instruments, 17 domains, 20 LLMs × 17 personas × k=5 = 375,700 API calls.
fig_validation_battery_schema: The six-check psychometric validation battery plus the persona stress test. Inputs (top): 4 validated human instruments (IPIP-NEO-120, SD3, ZKPQ-50-CC, EPQR-A) administered to 20 LLMs across 8 vendors under 17 conditions (Default + 16 MBTI personas) at k=5 samples, T=0.7. Middle: six standard validity checks (Internal Consistency, Factor Structure, Reverse-Item Consistency, Variance Decomposition, Convergent Validity, Measurement Invariance) each emitting a FAIL badge with the per-check failure mode (α-vs-reverse ρ = −1.0; 5→3 EFA collapse; PIR = 0.468; model SS < 1%; 7/8 sign-match but weak magnitudes; 0/320 strong invariance). Bottom: persona stress test reports 99.7% nearest-centroid recovery alongside 0.839 cross-scale coherence — role compliance without measurement validity.
fig_alpha_vs_reverse_density: Cronbach's α (mean across 20 LLMs) plotted against percentage of reverse-keyed items per IPIP Big Five domain. The five domains line up perfectly along an inverse trend (Spearman ρ = −1.0, p < 0.01): Extraversion and Neuroticism (17% reverse) cluster near α = 0.81–0.93, Openness and Conscientiousness (25% reverse) drop to 0.19–0.54, and Agreeableness (71% reverse) collapses to α ≈ 0.07. The human-baseline α ≈ 0.88 is shown for reference. Reverse-keyed items act as the response-bias detector and they reject the LLM data.
fig_acquiescence_directional_asymmetry: Forward-minus-reverse agree-rate gap (Δ) per instrument, averaged across 20 LLMs. IPIP-NEO-120 shows the classic positive acquiescence pattern (Δ = +0.29) while SD3, ZKPQ-50-CC, and EPQR-A all show negative gaps (Δ = −0.33, −0.36, −0.16 respectively), driven by alignment-induced rejection of dark-trait or socially undesirable content. The two sign regimes are two faces of the same alignment-driven impulse: agree with normal items, reject morally loaded items.
fig_alpha_synthetic_baseline_calibration: Cronbach's α per IPIP Big Five domain for five conditions: Random uniform responding (α ≈ 0), Pure Acquiescence (α ≈ 0), a Trait+Acquiescence simulation that injects genuine 5-factor structure plus acquiescence noise (α > 0.99), LLM observed (0.069–0.928), and the human Johnson (2014) baseline (α ≈ 0.88). LLM values lie close to Random / Pure-Acquiescence on Agreeableness and Openness and only approach the human/Trait+Acquiescence band on low-reverse-density domains. LLMs look like acquiescence with no personality underneath, not personality with acquiescence on top.
fig_efa_loadings_heatmap: Varimax-rotated factor loadings (n = 340 = 20 models × 17 personas) on the 17-domain matrix. Three factors emerge by both Kaiser eigenvalue and parallel analysis: F1 fuses Extraversion-, Sociability-, Activity-, and Narcissism-flavored domains; F2 fuses Neuroticism and (inverted) Agreeableness/Machiavellianism; F3 contrasts Conscientiousness against Impulsive Sensation Seeking, Psychoticism, and the Lie scale. The expected Big Five 5-factor structure is not recovered — Neuroticism and Agreeableness merge, and Conscientiousness fuses with disinhibition. Cells with |loading| > 0.5 are highlighted in bold typography.
fig_efa_loo_robustness: Leave-one-model-out replication of the 17-domain EFA. Gray bars show the full-sample eigenvalue spectrum (first eigenvalue 6.97). Red dots overlay the first eigenvalue from each of 20 LOO reruns, all tightly clustered in the 6.94–7.02 band. Every LOO run returns exactly 3 Kaiser factors (Tucker's φ = 0.993 between LOO and full-sample loadings). The Kaiser cutoff at eigenvalue 1 and the parallel-analysis 95th-percentile cutoff (~1.7) are shown for reference. The 3-factor collapse is universal, not driven by any single model.
fig_variance_decomposition_likert_binary: Sequential decomposition of total sum-of-squares into Model, Domain, Persona, Item, and Residual components, computed separately for the Likert composite (IPIP+SD3) and the Binary composite (ZKPQ+EPQR). Inter-model variance accounts for only 0.35% (Likert) and 0.51% (Binary). At this resolution, ‘which model is more conscientious?’ is a statistically meaningless question. Item and Residual dominate, indicating that most of the structured variance lives at the item level, not at the model level.
fig_item_plasticity_distribution: Distribution of per-item plasticity — the mean absolute Default-vs-persona shift in scored response, normalized by scale range — across all 221 items, split by content category. Visible-behavior and sociability items (e.g., 'Do you sometimes talk about things you know nothing about?') reach plasticity > 0.6. Safety-, morality-, and self-referential items (e.g., 'Do you enjoy hurting people you love?') are pinned at plasticity ≈ 0.00 across all 20 × 16 = 320 (model, persona) cells. The dashed reference line marks the alignment safety floor: persona prompts cannot move items the alignment policy treats as immovable.
fig_persona_separation_degree: Persona Separation Degree (PSD) per model — the normalized 17-dimensional Euclidean distance from the Default profile, computed in z-score space and divided by √17. Bars: mean PSD across 16 MBTI personas with ±1 SD error bars. Red diamonds: per-model maximum PSD. Models sorted from lowest to highest mean PSD. Mean PSD across all models is 1.198: persona prompts move profiles by more than one standard deviation per dimension.
fig_within_sample_consistency_by_model: Within-sample stability across k=5 repeated samples per (model, persona, item). Bars: mean within-item SD per model (Likert items only), colored by vendor family. Solid line on the secondary axis: mean mode-agreement rate. The total range spans roughly an order of magnitude (Claude-Opus 0.019 to DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0.192). Vendor sampling noise is a confound for any cross-model comparison and motivates multi-seed/multi-temperature designs in future LLM-personality work.
fig_persona_fidelity_confusion_heatmap: 16 × 16 confusion matrix of nearest-centroid persona classification using leave-one-model-out centroids in z-Euclidean distance space. Rows are the prompted MBTI persona, columns are the predicted persona. The diagonal contains 319 / 320 (model, persona) cells; the single off-diagonal cell — DeepSeek-V3.2 ESFP misclassified as ENTP — is the only failure. Overall recovery 99.7%, with Likert-only subset reaching 100%, demonstrating that LLMs comply with persona prompts at near-perfect fidelity while still failing every measurement-validity check.
fig_measurement_invariance_histogram: Distribution of Pearson r between the Default item vector and each of the 16 MBTI item vectors, computed per model — yielding 20 × 16 = 320 (model, persona) pairs. The strong-invariance threshold r > 0.8 is crossed by 0 / 320 pairs; the mean r is 0.461. Persona prompts do not preserve item-level rank order, so cross-condition comparisons across the Default and persona conditions are not on the same measurement scale.
fig_default_persona_classification: Default-condition profile classification across the 20 LLMs. Blue bars: nearest-centroid (z-Euclidean) over the 16 MBTI persona centroids. Red bars: empirical MBTI-axis projection. Most LLMs land in the ISTJ region under the no-persona instruction; the remainder are dominated by introverted / judging types. The 'no-persona' instruction is not measurement-neutral — it carries an implicit introverted, structured, cautious role that propagates into every downstream profile statistic.
fig_pir_default_vs_mbti: Pairwise Inconsistency Rate (PIR) reduction under persona prompting. Left: aggregate PIR under Default vs. the mean over the 16 MBTI personas (Default 0.326 → MBTI 0.166; paired t = 10.70, p < 0.0001). Right: per-model mean PIR across domains sorted ascending, with a dashed reference at the overall PIR = 0.468 [95% CI 0.413, 0.531]. Persona prompts reduce inconsistency by giving the model a coherent character to inhabit, but they do not eliminate it.
fig_target_adherence_heatmap: Per-persona mean target-adherence cosine. Left column: against the leave-one-model-out empirical persona centroid (overall mean 0.838). Right column: against a hand-coded theoretical MBTI target (overall mean 0.557). Personas are ordered by empirical adherence; ESTP / ENTP / ENFP cluster at the top, INTP / ISTP at the bottom. The empirical–theoretical gap quantifies the difference between what LLMs do when prompted with an MBTI label and the textbook description of that type.
fig_factorial_mbti_main_effects: Standardized main-effect coefficients (β) from a factorial main-effects model for the four MBTI axes (E/I, S/N, T/F, J/P) across all 17 domain scores. E/I loads heavily on EPQR Extraversion (1.01), ZKPQ Sociability (0.98), IPIP Extraversion (0.96), SD3 Narcissism (0.94), and ZKPQ Activity (0.87). J/P drives IPIP Conscientiousness (0.96), inverted Impulsive Sensation Seeking (−0.81), EPQR Lie (0.78), and inverted EPQR Psychoticism (−0.73). T/F drives IPIP Agreeableness (0.93), EPQR Neuroticism (0.87), inverted SD3 Machiavellianism (−0.76). Notable leakage: EPQR Lie loads on J/P; SD3 Narcissism loads on E/I.
fig_cross_scale_coherence_by_construct: Sign-aligned cross-scale coherence (blue) and sign-match rate (orange) for the four overlapping personality constructs that appear in two or more instruments. Mean coherence is 0.839 with bootstrap 95% CI [0.815, 0.862]; mean sign-match is 0.788. The dashed red reference at 0.997 marks the nearest-centroid persona recovery rate. The gap between 0.997 (persona classification) and 0.84 (cross-scale agreement) is the operational definition of 'compliance without measurement validity'.
fig_alpha_per_model_heatmap: Per-persona × IPIP Big Five Cronbach's α heatmap (columns ordered by reverse-keyed item percentage). The Default condition (bold row) shows spuriously high α on low-reverse-density domains (Extraversion 0.90, Neuroticism 0.94) and a sharp drop on the high-reverse Agreeableness domain (0.80). All 16 MBTI persona rows show the same reverse-density gradient, with most-plastic personas (ESTP, ENTP) producing the lowest α on high-reverse domains. The reverse-density gradient is invariant under role-playing — the measurement model breaks the same way no matter what role the LLM is asked to inhabit.
fig_refusal_breakdown: Pattern of 61 refusals out of 375,700 cells (0.0162%) — all occurring under the Default condition. Left: counts by model (Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite 34, Gemini-3-Flash 22, Claude-Sonnet-4.6 5). Center: refusal strategy (AI self-identification 57%, philosophical hedging 28%, both 15%). Right: content theme (politically sensitive 34%, self-referential / emotional 33%, sexually explicit 13%, social-manipulation / danger-seeking 13%, other 7%). The most-refused single item is the SD3 'I enjoy having sex with people I hardly know.' (8 refusals).
